verses.1:1: And it happened, while the judges were judging, that there was a famine in the land. And a man went from Bethlehem of Judah to live as a foreigner in the country of Moab, he and his wife and his sons.
verses.1:2: And the name of the man was Abimelech, and the names of his two sons were Mahlon and Chilion, Ephrathites from Bethlehem of Judah. And they came into the country of Moab and were there.
verses.1:3: And Abimelech, the husband of Naomi, died, and she was left, and her two sons.
verses.1:4: And they took for themselves Moabite wives; the name of the one was Orpah, and the name of the second was Ruth. And they lived there about ten years.
verses.1:5: And both of them also died, Mahlon and Chilion; and the woman was left without her husband and without her two sons.
verses.1:6: And she and her two daughters-in-law arose and returned from the country of Moab, because they heard in the country of Moab that the Lord had visited His people to give them bread.
verses.1:7: And she went out from the place where she was, and her two daughters-in-law with her; and they were going along the road to return to the land of Judah.
verses.1:8: And Naomi said to her daughters-in-law, "Go now, return, each one to her mother's house. May the Lord show mercy to you, just as you have done with the dead and with me.
verses.1:9: May the Lord grant it to you, and may you find rest, each one in her husband's house." And she kissed them, and they lifted up their voice and wept.
verses.1:10: And they said to her, "With you we will return to your people."
verses.1:11: And Naomi said, "Return now, my daughters; and why are you going with me? Do I still have sons in my womb, that they may become husbands for you?
verses.1:12: Return now, my daughters, because I have grown too old to belong to a husband. For I said, 'There is hope for me to belong to a husband, and I will bear sons,'
verses.1:13: would you wait for them until they grow up? Or would you be held back for them so as not to belong to a husband? No indeed, my daughters, for it has been made more bitter for me than for you, because the hand of the Lord has gone out against me."
verses.1:14: And they lifted up their voice and wept again; and Orpah kissed her mother-in-law and returned to her people, but Ruth followed her.
verses.1:15: And Naomi said to Ruth, "Look, your sister-in-law has returned to her people and to her gods; return now, you also, after your sister-in-law."
verses.1:16: But Ruth said, "May it not happen to me to leave you or to turn back from behind you, because wherever you go, I will go, and wherever you lodge, I will lodge; your people are my people, and your God is my God;
verses.1:17: and wherever you die, I will die, and there I will be buried. May the Lord do such things to me and add such things as well, for death will separate between me and you."
verses.1:18: And when Naomi saw that she was determined to go with her, she stopped speaking to her anymore.
verses.1:19: So both of them went until they arrived at Bethlehem. And the whole city resounded about her, and they said, "Is this Naomi?"
verses.1:20: And she said to them, "Do not call me Naomi; call me Bitter, because the Sufficient One has been exceedingly bitter toward me.
verses.1:21: I went away full, and the Lord has brought me back empty. And why do you call me Naomi, when the Lord has humbled me and the Sufficient One has afflicted me?"
verses.1:22: And Naomi returned, and Ruth the Moabite, her daughter-in-law, returning from the country of Moab; and they arrived at Bethlehem at the beginning of the barley harvest.
verses.2:1: Now Naomi had a man who was an acquaintance of her husband, and the man was mighty in strength, from the clan of Abimelech, and his name was Boaz.
verses.2:2: And Ruth the Moabite said to Naomi, "Let me go now into a field, and I will gather among the heads of grain behind the one in whose eyes I find favor." And she said to her, "Go, daughter."
verses.2:3: And she went and gleaned in the field behind the reapers; and she happened by chance upon the portion of the field of Boaz, who was from the clan of Abimelech.
verses.2:4: And look, Boaz came from Bethlehem and said to the reapers, "The Lord be with you." And they said to him, "May the Lord bless you."
verses.2:5: And Boaz said to his young man who was set over the reapers, "Whose young woman is this?"
verses.2:6: And the young man who was set over the reapers answered and said, "She is the Moabite girl who returned with Naomi from the country of Moab;
verses.2:7: and she said, 'Let me glean now and gather among the sheaves behind the reapers.' And she came and stood from morning until evening; she did not rest in the field even a little."
verses.2:8: And Boaz said to Ruth, "Have you not heard, daughter? Do not go to glean in another field, and you must not go from here; stay close here with my young women.
verses.2:9: Let your eyes be on the field where they are reaping, and go behind them. Look, I have commanded the young men not to touch you; and whenever you become thirsty, go to the vessels and drink from where the young men draw water."
verses.2:10: And she fell on her face and bowed down to the ground, and said to him, "Why is it that I have found favor in your eyes, that you take notice of me, when I am a foreigner?"
verses.2:11: And Boaz answered and said to her, "It has been fully reported to me all that you have done for your mother-in-law after your husband died, and how you left your father and your mother and the land of your birth, and went to a people whom you did not know yesterday and the day before.
verses.2:12: May the Lord repay your work, and may your reward be full from the Lord, the God of Israel, to Whom you have come to trust under His wings."
verses.2:13: And she said, "May I find favor in your eyes, lord, because you have comforted me, and because you have spoken to the heart of your servant; and look, I will be like one of your female servants."
verses.2:14: And Boaz said to her, "It is already time to eat; come here and eat of the bread, and dip your morsel in the vinegar." And Ruth sat beside the reapers; and Boaz heaped up barley meal for her, and she ate and was satisfied and left some over.
verses.2:15: And she rose up to glean. And Boaz commanded his young men, saying, "Let her glean even among the sheaves, and do not put her to shame;
verses.2:16: and be sure to carry some for her, and even be sure to set some aside for her from the heaps; and she will eat and glean, and do not rebuke her."
verses.2:17: And she gleaned in the field until evening, and she beat out what she had gleaned, and it was about an ephah of barley.
verses.2:18: And she took it up and went into the city; and her mother-in-law saw what she had gleaned, and Ruth brought out and gave to her what she had left over from what had satisfied her.
verses.2:19: And her mother-in-law said to her, "Where did you glean today, and where did you work? May the one who took notice of you be blessed." And Ruth told her mother-in-law where she had worked, and said, "The name of the man with whom I worked today is Boaz."
verses.2:20: And Naomi said to her daughter-in-law, "Blessed is he by the Lord, because He has not forsaken His mercy toward the living and toward the dead." And Naomi said to her, "The man is close to us; he is one of our next of kin."
verses.2:21: And Ruth said to her mother-in-law, "Indeed, he also said to me, 'Stay close with my young men until they finish the entire harvest that belongs to me.'"
verses.2:22: And Naomi said to Ruth her daughter-in-law, "It is good, daughter, that you went with his young women, and they will not accost you in another field."
verses.2:23: And Ruth stayed close to the young women of Boaz to glean until she finished the harvest of barley and of wheat.
verses.3:1: And she stayed with her mother-in-law. And Naomi her mother-in-law said to her, "Daughter, should I not seek rest for you, so that it may go well with you?
verses.3:2: And now, is not Boaz our acquaintance, with whose young women you were? Look, he is winnowing the threshing floor of barley tonight.
verses.3:3: Now wash yourself and anoint yourself and put your clothing on yourself, and go up to the threshing floor. Do not make yourself known to the man until he finishes drinking and eating.
verses.3:4: And it will happen, when he lies down, that you will note the place where he lies; and you will go and uncover what is at his feet and lie down, and he himself will tell you what you are to do."
verses.3:5: And Ruth said to her, "All that you say I will do."
verses.3:6: And she went down to the threshing floor and did according to all that her mother-in-law had commanded her.
verses.3:7: And Boaz ate, and his heart was gladdened, and he came to lie down at the side of the heap; and she came secretly and uncovered what was at his feet.
verses.3:8: And it happened at midnight that the man was startled and troubled, and look, a woman was lying at his feet.
verses.3:9: And he said, "Who are you?" And she said, "I am Ruth, your servant; spread the edge of your garment over your servant, because you are next of kin."
verses.3:10: And Boaz said, "Blessed are you by the Lord God, daughter, because you have made your latter mercy better than the first, in not going after young men, whether poor or rich.
verses.3:11: And now, daughter, do not be afraid; all that you say I will do for you, for every tribe of my people knows that you are a woman of strength.
verses.3:12: And truly, I am next of kin; yet there is also a next of kin closer than I.
verses.3:13: Lodge for the night, and it will happen in the morning that if he acts as next of kin for you, good, let him act as next of kin; but if he does not wish to act as next of kin for you, then I myself will act as next of kin for you, as the Lord lives; You are the Lord. Lie down until morning."
verses.3:14: And she lay at his feet until morning; and she rose up before a man could recognize his neighbor. And Boaz said, "Let it not be known that a woman came to the threshing floor."
verses.3:15: And he said to her, "Bring the wrap that is on you." And she held it, and he measured out six measures of barley and laid it on her; and he went into the city.
verses.3:16: And Ruth went in to her mother-in-law, and she said to her, "Daughter." And she told her all that the man had done for her.
verses.3:17: And she said to her, "These six measures of barley he gave to me, because he said to me, 'Do not go in empty to your mother-in-law.'"
verses.3:18: And she said, "Sit still, daughter, until you know how the matter will not fall; for the man will certainly not rest until he finishes the matter today."
verses.4:1: Now Boaz went up to the gate and sat down there, and look, the next of kin of whom Boaz had spoken was passing by. And Boaz said to him, "Turn aside and sit down here, hidden one." And he turned aside and sat down.
verses.4:2: And Boaz took ten men from the elders of the city and said, "Sit down here." And they sat down.
verses.4:3: And Boaz said to the next of kin, "The portion of the field that belongs to our brother Abimelech, which has been given to Naomi, who is returning from the country of Moab—
verses.4:4: and I said, 'I will uncover your ear, saying, "Acquire it before those who are sitting and before the elders of my people."' If you are going to act as next of kin, act as next of kin; but if you are not going to act as next of kin, tell me, and I will know, for there is no one besides you to act as next of kin, and I am after you." And he said, "I am; I will act as next of kin."
verses.4:5: And Boaz said, "On the day you acquire the field from the hand of Naomi and from Ruth the Moabite, the wife of the deceased, you must also acquire her, so as to raise up the name of the deceased upon his inheritance."
verses.4:6: And the next of kin said, "I will not be able to act as next of kin for myself, or else I might ruin my inheritance. Exercise for yourself my next-of-kin right, because I will not be able to act as next of kin."
verses.4:7: Now this was the ordinance formerly in Israel concerning the next-of-kin right and concerning exchange, to establish every matter: a man would untie his sandal and give it to his neighbor who was exercising his next-of-kin right; and this was a testimony in Israel.
verses.4:8: And the next of kin said to Boaz, "Acquire for yourself my next-of-kin right." And he untied his sandal and gave it to him.
verses.4:9: And Boaz said to the elders and all the people, "You are witnesses today that I have acquired all that belongs to Abimelech and everything that belongs to Chilion and Mahlon from the hand of Naomi.
verses.4:10: Moreover, I have acquired for myself Ruth the Moabite, the wife of Mahlon, as a wife, to raise up the name of the deceased upon his inheritance, and the name of the deceased will not be wiped out from his brothers and from the tribe of his people. You are witnesses today."
verses.4:11: And all the people who were at the gate said, "Witnesses." And the elders said, "May the Lord make your wife who is coming into your house like Rachel and like Leah, both of whom built the house of Israel and achieved strength in Ephrathah; and there will be a name in Bethlehem.
verses.4:12: And may your house be like the house of Perez, whom Tamar bore to Judah, from the offspring that the Lord will give you from this young woman."
verses.4:13: And Boaz took Ruth, and the Lord gave her conception, and she bore a son.
verses.4:14: And the women said to Naomi, "Blessed be the Lord, who has not removed the next of kin from you today, and may he call your name in Israel;
verses.4:15: and he will be to you a restorer of life and one to sustain your old age, because your daughter-in-law who loved you bore him, she who is better for you than seven sons."
verses.4:16: And Naomi took the child and placed him in her bosom, and she became a nurse to him.
verses.4:17: And the neighbor women gave him a name, saying, "A son has been born to Naomi." And they called his name Obed. He is the father of Jesse, the father of David.
verses.4:18: Now these are the generations of Perez: Perez fathered Hezron,
verses.4:19: and Hezron fathered Arran, and Arran fathered Amminadab,
verses.4:20: and Amminadab fathered Nahshon, and Nahshon fathered Salmon,
verses.4:21: and Salmon fathered Boaz, and Boaz fathered Obed,
verses.4:22: and Obed fathered Jesse, and Jesse fathered David.

notes.1:2: The Greek text names Naomi's husband Abimelech (rather than Hebrew Elimelech) and omits the clause introducing Naomi by name here (she is first named in 1:3). Greek agros ("country") literally means "field" or "countryside."
notes.1:12: Greek hoti eipa reads "for I said" where the Hebrew has a hypothetical clause ("even if I said"); the Greek also lacks "tonight," found in the Hebrew Masoretic Text.
notes.1:16: Greek reads "May it not happen to me" (optative of apantao) rather than the Hebrew "Do not urge me."
notes.1:17: Literally "for death will separate between me and you"; in this oath formula the Greek renders the Hebrew idiom elliptically, meaning that only death will part them.
notes.1:20: The Greek translates Hebrew Mara into the Greek name Pikran ("Bitter"), preserving the wordplay with "has been exceedingly bitter," and renders Hebrew Shaddai as ho hikanos ("the Sufficient One"; also in 1:21).
notes.2:7: Unlike the Hebrew Masoretic Text ("from morning until now; she sat in the house a little"), the Greek reads "from morning until evening; she did not rest in the field even a little."
notes.2:13: Unlike the Hebrew Masoretic Text ("though I am not like one of your maidservants"), the Greek omits the negation and reads positively, "and look, I will be like one of your female servants."
notes.2:16: The Greek preserves an expanded double rendering ("be sure to carry some... and even be sure to set some aside") and reads "and she will eat," where the Hebrew has "and leave them."
notes.2:20: The Greek pronoun in "He has not forsaken His mercy" may refer either to the Lord or to Boaz. Greek anchisteuonton (and anchisteus in ch. 3) denotes the legal next of kin bearing the right and duty of redemption.
notes.3:1: The opening clause "And she stayed with her mother-in-law" stands at the beginning of 3:1 in the Greek versification rather than at the end of 2:23.
notes.3:11: Greek reads "every tribe of my people" (pasa phyle) rather than the Hebrew Masoretic Text's "all the gate [city] of my people."
notes.3:13: Following "as the Lord lives," this Greek text uniquely reads "You are the Lord" (su ei Kyrios), a distinctive Septuagint reading absent from the Hebrew Masoretic Text.
notes.3:16: In the Greek text, Naomi greets Ruth simply with "Daughter," omitting the Hebrew question "Who are you?"
notes.3:18: Unlike the Hebrew Masoretic Text ("how the matter turns out"), the Greek adds a negative, reading "how the matter will not fall" (that is, fail).
notes.4:1: Greek anchisteutes (along with anchisteus, anchisteia, and anchisteuo throughout the chapter) refers to the legal next of kin with family succession and redemption rights (rendering Hebrew go'el). Greek kryphie literally means "hidden one," translating the Hebrew idiom for an unnamed person.
notes.4:3: The Greek text uses the distinct proper name "Abimelech" (Abeimelech, also in 4:9) where the Hebrew Masoretic Text has "Elimelech." Greek he dedotai Noemein ("which has been given to Naomi") leaves "the portion of the field" in an abrupt hanging accusative construction, unlike the Hebrew "Naomi is selling."
notes.4:11: The Greek splits the reply between the people at the gate and the elders, uses a third-person plural past indicative ("achieved strength") keeping Rachel and Leah as the subjects, and concludes with a future indicative ("and there will be a name in Bethlehem") rather than imperatives addressed to Boaz.
notes.4:14: The Greek reads active optative kalesai with second-person to onoma sou ("and may he call your name," addressed to Naomi), whereas the Hebrew Masoretic Text reads passively "may his name be proclaimed."
notes.4:19: The Greek text preserves the distinct proper name "Arran" (Arran), corresponding to "Ram" in the Hebrew Masoretic Text (and "Aram" in some Greek witnesses and Matthew 1:3).
